ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A personal story: one of the colony's named animals and this colonist have taken against each other, often after it stole their food. It passes in a few days, and the story ends in a grudging truce. Eating at a table, with the food put away, gives the animal fewer chances.

The council chose between the herd and the stores in a hungry week. It fades in a few days. A herd no bigger than the fields and the hay can feed, and food stored ahead of winter, keep the question from coming up.
A wild animal ate the crops they'd grown. It passes in a few days. A fence round the fields keeps grazers out, and a hunt or a night's watch settles the next one.

The council decided how much medicine a sick animal was worth. It fades in a few days. More medicine in store, herbal at the least, makes the next answer easier; the greedy and the cold-hearted mind any medicine spent on an animal.

The council settled a quarrel between a bond with an animal and a faith that frowns on it. It fades in a few days, except giving the animal to someone else, which hurts its person for eight. Keeping the animal out of the faithful one's way hurts nobody much.

A predator got into the pens, or one of the herd was lost on the grazing. It passes in a few days. Pens close to the houses, a barn with a door, and a hunt or a watch when something stalks the herd keep it from happening again.
Their Pokémon went down in a fight. It lasts a day. Tending it, or a potion, gets it on its feet; keeping a low-level Pokémon back from the worst fighting avoids it.
The council let a rare Pokémon pass by. It lasts two days and is very slight. Going out to see the next one, or sending the colony's trainer after it, turns it into a good memory instead.
